explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/1092 with Rödl's negative answer. 'f_2(n) ≫ n', where f_2 is the maximal admissible function, is encoded as the existence of an admissible g with g(n) ≥ cn eventually. This is equivalent, because admissibility is downward closed. The negation holds even though g may be tiny for small m. Rödl's graphs (χ ≥ k, every m-vertex subgraph bipartite after deleting εm edges) with ε < c and ε < 1/M have all subgraphs on fewer than M vertices already bipartite, so they meet the hypothesis for any such g while having chromatic number > 3.
